newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices mixed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices mixed in dull trade.

text.p: Sugar prices were mixed on Monday in the absence of demand from local consumers and those in other centres, especially southern India, dealers said.
Ready sugar S-30 fell 5.0/7.0 rupees to 1,410/1,448 rupees per quintal (100 kg). Sugar M-30, however, gained 5.0 rupees to 1,465/1,505 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery was steady at 1,465/1,475 rupees per quintal for new quality.
Dealers said bulk demand from soft drink and ice cream makers from south India had also come down with the four-month June-September monsoon approaching nearer.
Weather reports indicated a delay of seven to 10 days in the arrival of monsoon rains, dealers said.
Dealers said the market was also awaiting the release of free sale sugar quota for the July-September quarter.
"There could be some movement in the market once the free sale quota is announced," said a trader. The government had released 2.17 million tonnes for the quarter ending June.
